title: Polylingy course, format 10
description: The shape of course.json. The app checks more than this schema can say (markup, blanks per item, links pointing at real sections, model answers passing their keys): run ./gradlew :app:checkCourse. See docs/content-format.md.

uuid.description: A UUID. Ids may be left out in a file: the app adds them on import.

inline.description: Text with markup: **bold**, *italic*, a highlight ==marked== (=={2}second== style: after the opening == the number of the palette's mark in braces, 1 to 5; none means 1), line breaks \n, annotated words [word](annotation) shown with the annotation over them; in exercises blanks {{answer|other variant}}. \\ makes the next * = { } | [ ] \\ literal. See content-format.md, section 3.

audio.description: A sound: an https:// URL or a path inside the course archive (audio/hello.mp3); .mp3 or .wav. It plays when its button is pressed.

image.description: A picture: an https:// URL or a path inside the course archive (images/cat.png). alt describes it.

description.description: What exactly is in the picture, in words, for editors and tools; the app does not show it.

made.description: How the picture was made (the prompt of an image model, or the script and data of a drawing); the app does not show it.

course.description: A course file (course.json). It has either units or topics, not both.

formatVersion.description: The format this file is written in. This schema describes 13.

version.description: The version of the course's content: 1 for the first, one more with every change (in the app, or by a newer file). A file of a course already in the app updates it only when this is higher than the stored one. Without it, 1.

extraKeys.description: Keys the course adds to every text field because the keyboard has none for them, e.g. letters of the language: shown above the field while it has focus.

unit.description: A part of a course: a page of theory and the topics that practise it.

topic.description: The unit of spaced repetition; each time it is shown, one of its exercises is picked.

rules.description: Study settings the course starts with: a preset and the parts that differ from it. See learning-model.md.

display.description: How the course looks and how exercises are shown: annotations over words shown (default true); avoid exercises that need typing when a topic has others (default false); the palette (an id from the app's list, see content-format.md; left out: the app's default) and the style (soft, the default: marks on a coloured background; strict: marks underlined).

palette.description: The id of the colour palette: softGreen, paperAndInk, blue, terracotta, pine or plum. An id this version does not know is drawn in the default palette.

style.description: strict (default): marks underlined, no background; soft: marks on a coloured background.

grading.all-correct.description: Right when every item is right.

grading.threshold.description: Right when at least min of the items are right.

mastery.consecutive.description: Learned after this many right answers in a row.

scheduler.ladder.description: Reviews after these days; without retire the last gap doubles.

picker.conveyor.description: Stays on a topic until its round is done.

exercise.description: Which exercise of a topic comes next: random-not-last (default): a random one, never the one answered last; in-order: one after another in the order of the course, round and round; missed-first: first the one missed longest ago and not answered right since, but never in the round it was missed in, then in order.

Which exercise of a topic comes next: random-not-last (default): a random one, never the one answered last; in-order: one after another in the order of the course, round and round; missed-first: first the one missed longest ago and not answered right since, but never in the round it was missed in, then in order.

Which exercise of a topic comes next: random-not-last (default): a random one, never the one answered last; in-order: one after another in the order of the course, round and round; missed-first: first the one missed longest ago and not answered right since, but never in the round it was missed in, then in order.

content.description: A page of content: unit theory or an explanation.

block.description: A building block of a content page, told apart by "type".

block.section.description: A part of a page: with a label (a letter) it is lettered in the margin; without one its title is a heading. id is set only on sections a seeAlso link points at.

block.text.description: A paragraph. A role says what it is for: a lead is the introduction of the part it opens.

role.description: What the paragraph is for; the app decides how it looks.

block.situation.description: An example situation, with an optional aside block (usually a picture).

look.description: How the situation is set off from the text: a soft card (default) or no frame.

frame.description: The frame of an exercise's text (an email, an article, a newspaper clipping) drawn around the situation.

description.description: What exactly is in the picture, in words, for editors and tools; the app does not show it.

made.description: How the picture was made (the prompt of an image model, or the script and data of a drawing); the app does not show it.

size.description: How big the picture is: a word, not pixels; the same words as an exercise's aside.

cell.description: A theory table cell: a text, or {text, rowSpan, audio}; a cell with audio shows a play button and may leave text out.

oneOf.description: A cell spanning rows, or with a sound.

block.table.description: A table; all rows have the same number of columns, counting cells spanned from above.

line.description: One remark of a dialogue: who says it, what, its sound, and its translation (small and grey under it; the course decides where one helps).

block.track.description: A recording of its own, as a book prints it beside a section: one sound with a title. A long one plays in the player docked at the bottom of the window, where it can be paused and rewound.

block.video.description: A video on the web, which the app opens in the browser: the course points to it, it does not carry it.

block.dialogue.description: A conversation, one line per remark with the speaker's name on the left and an optional sound.

look.description: Lines in a column with the names on the left (default), or speech bubbles: the first speaker on the left, the second on the right.

portraits.description: A picture for each speaker; shown next to the bubbles.

block.quote.description: A line of speech in a bubble.

example.description: One example; not is the wrong form to contrast with; translation shows small and grey under it; audio gives it a play button.

block.tip.description: A remark set apart from the text; kind says what sort of remark it is.

kind.description: The sort of remark; default tip. fact is "Did you know?", culture a custom or a tradition.

title.description: A heading instead of the kind's caption.

aside.description: A block (usually a picture) beside the remark.

link.description: A link to a theory section (its id) or to the top of a unit's theory (its id).

exercise.description: An exercise, told apart by "type". Every type has the same layers: instruction, wordBank (some types), audio, look, aside, the body (the type's own fields), explanation. See content-format.md, section 5.

look.description: Layer 3: a frame with a header around the body. Fits every exercise type.

look.email.description: An email: subject on top, then the sender (with an initial) and the recipient.

look.article.description: A page of a magazine, newspaper or blog: a small source line over the title.

look.newspaper.description: A newspaper clipping: the headline, big and bold in a dotted frame, with a small source line (the paper, the day) over it.

aside.description: Layer 4: one picture next to the body, inside the frame when there is a look. side and size are words: left/right take ¼, ⅓, ½ of the width (small, medium, large), top/bottom ⅓, ½, all of it; the picture keeps its proportions.

video.description: Layer 3b: a video on the web, shown as a card over the exercise; the app opens its address in the browser. Same fields as the video block of a theory page, without type.

exercise.gaps.description: Sentences with blanks to type into. Each blank is one item; one item may hold a whole text with many blanks.

passage.description: A page of blocks the exercise is about (a dialogue, a story, a letter), shown above the frame as in the unit theory; original text only.

generated.description: True when the exercise was generated, not written by the course's author; default false.

gapItem.description: text has at least one blank {{answer|variant}} (each variant at most 60 characters), which may carry a hint {{answer}}[[hint]] shown in grey in the empty field; note under a wrong answer.

exercise.choice.description: An option is picked in each place. Each place is one item.

passage.description: A page of blocks the exercise is about (a dialogue, a story, a letter), shown above the frame as in the unit theory; original text only.

generated.description: True when the exercise was generated, not written by the course's author; default false.

choiceItem.description: Either one blank holding the right answer plus options, or no options and any number of blanks each listing its options, right one first: {{admit|’m admitting}}.

mark.description: A piece of text this item is about; once the exercise is checked, choosing the item marks it in the text of the frame (look).

exercise.pictures.description: Picture cards, each with a sentence with blanks.

passage.description: A page of blocks the exercise is about (a dialogue, a story, a letter), shown above the frame as in the unit theory; original text only.

generated.description: True when the exercise was generated, not written by the course's author; default false.

pictureItem.description: A picture and a sentence with at least one blank.

exercise.table.description: A table with blanks in its cells; at least one blank.

passage.description: A page of blocks the exercise is about (a dialogue, a story, a letter), shown above the frame as in the unit theory; original text only.

generated.description: True when the exercise was generated, not written by the course's author; default false.

side.description: A side of a pair: a text, or {image}.

exercise.match.description: Pairs to match; right sides and extra are shown shuffled.

passage.description: A page of blocks the exercise is about (a dialogue, a story, a letter), shown above the frame as in the unit theory; original text only.

generated.description: True when the exercise was generated, not written by the course's author; default false.

exercise.order.description: Sentences to build from their shuffled words.

passage.description: A page of blocks the exercise is about (a dialogue, a story, a letter), shown above the frame as in the unit theory; original text only.

generated.description: True when the exercise was generated, not written by the course's author; default false.

orderItem.description: Either answer — a sentence built from its words (accept lists other right orders of the same words) — or parts — whole phrases, given in the right order, to put in order.

exercise.sort.description: Words to sort into groups: the words are shown shuffled in one pile, the learner puts each into its group.

passage.description: A page of blocks the exercise is about (a dialogue, a story, a letter), shown above the frame as in the unit theory; original text only.

generated.description: True when the exercise was generated, not written by the course's author; default false.

sortGroup.description: A group and the words that belong to it; each word is in one group only, and 3 to 24 words in all.

exercise.expand.description: Replies to write from notes (the word bank). An answer is right when it has the key words of one of the orders, in that order, with any words between them.

passage.description: A page of blocks the exercise is about (a dialogue, a story, a letter), shown above the frame as in the unit theory; original text only.

generated.description: True when the exercise was generated, not written by the course's author; default false.

expandItem.description: text has exactly one blank: the model answer (variants allowed, at most 150 characters), which must itself pass the keys. keys: allowed orders of the same key words or phrases, in the forms the answer needs.

exercise.fix.description: Texts with marked words: {{right as it is}} or {{wrong => fix|other fix}}. Each mark is one item: keep a right word, fix a wrong one.

passage.description: A page of blocks the exercise is about (a dialogue, a story, a letter), shown above the frame as in the unit theory; original text only.

generated.description: True when the exercise was generated, not written by the course's author; default false.

fixItem.description: A text with at least one mark.

portrait.description: A speaker's picture; who is the name as written in the lines' who.

block.grid.description: Blocks side by side in 2 to 4 columns; on a narrow window one under another.

table.appearance.description: How the table is drawn. Every field is optional; with none of them the table is as wide as its place, in a soft card, with thin lines between the rows, a plain header and no highlighted columns.

widthOfTable.description: fullWidth (default): the columns share the whole width of the page; onlyAsWideAsContent: every column is as wide as its text.

background.description: card (default): a soft card with an edge round the table; none: the table stands straight on the page.

headerRow.description: plain (default): header text in the accent colour over a line; highlighted: the header row is filled with the accent's soft tint.

highlightedColumns.description: Numbers of columns, the first is 0, drawn bold on a soft background.

stripedRows.description: Every other body row on a soft background.

linesBetweenRows.description: Thin lines between the body rows.
